Experimental electrophysiology demonstrates potent, use-dependent inhibition of hERG channels. Its protonatable tertiary piperidine nitrogen and extensive hydrophobic aromatic regions support membrane partitioning and interactions with aromatic residues Y652 and F656 in the hERG inner pore. Blockade reduces the rapid delayed rectifier potassium current (IKr), prolonging cardiac repolarization and increasing the risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes. Its active metabolite desmethylastemizole also inhibits hERG. Terfenadine is a potent hERG blocker with a reported IC50 of approximately 56 nM (0.056 μM). Its lipophilic structure contains two aromatic regions and a basic piperidine-containing side chain. These features favor membrane partitioning and interactions within the hydrophobic hERG channel cavity. Blockade of IKr delays ventricular repolarization and increases the probability of acquired long QT syndrome and torsades de pointes. The risk becomes particularly important when metabolism through CYP3A4 is inhibited, because increased parent-drug exposure can produce clinically significant cardiac toxicity. Tox21 activity cannot be reliably established from structural information alone. MMP and p53 could be investigated as exploratory endpoints, but neither is confirmed positive. The estimated IC50 is supported by PMID:9395068. Final opinion: do not proceed without resolving the established cardiac liability through structural modification, exposure assessment, and comprehensive electrophysiological testing.

Predicted hERG Blocker Probability: 0.99 (High Confidence). Mechanistic & Biological Basis: Astemizole is a prototypical, ultra-potent hERG (Kv11.1) potassium channel blocker with an experimental patch-clamp IC50 of approximately 0.9 nM (0.0009 uM, PMID:9843990; ChEMBL:CHEMBL294). Structurally, it features a central basic piperidine nitrogen flanked by lipophilic aromatic domains (4-fluorobenzylbenzimidazole and 4-methoxyphenethyl). At physiological pH, the protonated piperidine forms cation-pi interactions with Tyr652 and high-affinity hydrophobic/pi-stacking interactions with Phe656 inside the inner pore cavity of the hERG channel, stabilizing the inactivated state and severely delaying cardiac repolarization (IKr). Tox21 Profile: Due to its high lipophilicity (cLogP > 5) and cationic amphiphilic nature, Astemizole triggers mitochondrial membrane potential disruption (SR-MMP) and p53-mediated cellular stress (SR-p53), alongside off-target nuclear receptor LBD antagonism at micromolar concentrations. Limitations: In silico models cannot capture the toxicokinetics of its major active metabolite, desmethylastemizole, which exhibits a prolonged systemic half-life (~9-13 days) and accumulates in myocardial tissue. Final Safety Opinion: Do not proceed to clinical trials; Astemizole was withdrawn globally due to fatal ventricular arrhythmias and Torsades de Pointes (TdP).

Predicted hERG Blocker Probability: 0.99 (High Confidence). Mechanistic & Biological Basis: Terfenadine is a benchmark hERG potassium channel blocker with a mammalian cell patch-clamp IC50 of approximately 56 nM (0.056 uM, PMID:8620042; ChEMBL:CHEMBL17157). Its structure exemplifies the classic hERG pharmacophore: a protonatable tertiary piperidine amine linked to a bulky diphenylmethanol group on one side and a tert-butylphenyl-butanol chain on the other. This geometry allows deep insertion into the hERG central cavity, engaging Tyr652 and Phe656 via aromatic stacking and hydrophobic contacts that occlude potassium ion flux. Tox21 Profile: As a potent cationic amphiphilic molecule, Terfenadine induces mitochondrial depolarization (SR-MMP), oxidative stress signaling (SR-ARE), and p53 activation (SR-p53), along with promiscuous estrogen receptor interference (NR-ER) near cytotoxic thresholds. Limitations: Standard structure-based QSAR models evaluate only the parent molecule and do not inherently account for metabolic clearance; in vivo, Terfenadine undergoes rapid CYP3A4-mediated oxidation to fexofenadine (a zwitterion with negligible hERG affinity), meaning clinical cardiotoxicity manifests primarily during CYP3A4 inhibition or hepatic impairment. Final Safety Opinion: Do not proceed; the parent compound carries an unacceptable risk of QT prolongation and fatal Torsades de Pointes.
